description: Phase 1/2 shipped model, seed 123 (best of 3 seeds 42/123/2024)
notes: Reference point. Clean-test-set accuracy is real but doesn't reflect production: inference always applies crop_to_content, train/eval never did (see audit Finding 1).

description: Apply crop_to_content in train+eval too, matching inference exactly (get_transforms(content_crop=True))
notes: Fixes audit Finding 1. Clean test accuracy improved too (96.42%->97.87%), not just robustness. Robustness benchmark clean-condition 40.25%->97.25%; mean across 11 conditions 29.91%->82.29%. Promoted to models/symbol_classifier_v1 (production). thin_stroke condition still weak (1.0%->4.0%, 35/400 no-prediction) -- erosion on already-thin native strokes deletes them; flagged for a future stroke-thickness-specific experiment, not blocking this decision.

description: Add RandomStrokeWidth (p=0.3 dilate/erode) to training augmentation, to address user-reported div/minus bias under stroke-thickness shift (see experiments/div_bias_investigation/FINDINGS.md)
notes: Regressed clean test accuracy (97.87%->94.90%) and macro F1 (0.945->0.912) relative to exp1. Not evaluated further (robustness benchmark not run) because superseded mid-experiment by a product decision to remove 'div' from the vocabulary entirely (mathematicians use fractions, not the division-sign glyph) rather than fix classifier bias for a symbol being dropped. Recorded for completeness, not pursued.

description: Remove '\div' from the vocabulary (25 classes). Mathematicians use fractions, not the division-sign glyph; div was also the largest single source of the stroke-thickness bias exp2 tried and failed to fix by augmentation instead.
notes: Promoted to models/symbol_classifier_v1 (production). div-specific bias gone by construction. thick_stroke robustness improved (exp1: 64.5% -> 68.8%, errors now spread across classes instead of piling onto div). thin_stroke NOT resolved -- 'minus' (lowest ink-density class in the vocabulary, 0.061 mean ink fraction) is now the concentrated sink (248/300 wrong predictions land on it), same root cause as exp2 (no stroke-width augmentation), just relocated since div is gone. Documented as an open problem in README rather than claimed fixed. macro_f1 lower than exp1 mostly reflects 'x' having an unusually bad draw this seed (30% recall, n=10) -- known high seed-variance for that class, not evidence of a regression from removing div.
